structures.title: Basic statement word order (V2)
structures.explanation: In a German main clause the conjugated verb is always the second element, no matter what comes first. If a time or place opens the sentence, the subject moves after the verb so the verb stays in slot two.

structures.title: Forming questions
structures.explanation: Yes/no questions move the conjugated verb to the front, before the subject. For open questions a question word (was, wo, wann) takes first place and the verb still comes second.

structures.title: Negating with nicht
structures.explanation: nicht negates a verb, an adjective or a whole statement. It comes after the conjugated verb and its objects but before an adjective, a place phrase, or a final infinitive.

structures.title: Negating nouns with kein
structures.explanation: Use kein (not nicht) to negate a noun that has ein or no article. kein takes the same endings as ein and changes for gender and case.

structures.title: Modal verb bracket
structures.explanation: A modal verb sits in second position and its main verb, an infinitive, jumps to the very end of the clause. This 'verb bracket' frames the sentence.
structures.ex2_ref: We want to buy a house.

structures.title: Separable verbs split
structures.explanation: A separable verb splits in a main clause: the conjugated stem stays in position two and the prefix flies to the end. The two pieces bracket the rest of the sentence.

structures.title: Subordinate clause, verb to the end
structures.explanation: Subordinating conjunctions such as weil (because) and dass (that) push the conjugated verb to the end of their clause. A comma always separates the two clauses.
structures.ex1_target: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
structures.ex1_ref: I'm staying home because I'm ill.
structures.ex2_target: Ich glaube, dass er recht hat.
structures.ex2_ref: I think that he is right.

structures.title: Unreal (second) conditional
structures.explanation: For hypothetical situations use wenn with a Konjunktiv II verb (hätte, wäre, könnte) and würde + infinitive in the main clause. It expresses what would happen if things were different.
structures.ex1_target: Wenn ich Zeit hätte, würde ich kommen.
structures.ex1_ref: If I had time, I would come.
structures.ex2_target: Wenn ich reich wäre, würde ich reisen.
structures.ex2_ref: If I were rich, I would travel.

structures.title: Comparing two things
structures.explanation: Add -er to the adjective and follow it with als (than). Short root vowels a/o/u usually gain an umlaut (groß→größer, alt→älter).
structures.ex1_ref: He is taller than I am.
structures.ex2_target: Heute ist es kälter als gestern.
structures.ex2_ref: Today it is colder than yesterday.

structures.title: Relative clause
structures.explanation: A relative clause describes a noun and is introduced by der/die/das matching the noun's gender and number; its case depends on its role inside the clause, and the verb goes to the end.
structures.ex1_target: Der Mann, der dort wohnt, ist Arzt.
structures.ex1_ref: The man who lives there is a doctor.
structures.ex2_target: Das Buch, das ich lese, ist gut.
structures.ex2_ref: The book that I am reading is good.

structures.title: Saying there is / there are
structures.explanation: Es gibt means both 'there is' and 'there are' and is always followed by the accusative case. It never changes for singular or plural.
structures.ex1_target: Es gibt einen Park in der Nähe.

structures.title: Expressing purpose (in order to)
structures.explanation: um … zu + infinitive expresses purpose, answering 'why / what for'. The subject of both clauses must be the same; the infinitive with zu goes to the end.
structures.ex1_target: Ich lerne Deutsch, um in Berlin zu arbeiten.
structures.ex1_ref: I study German in order to work in Berlin.
structures.ex2_target: Sie spart Geld, um ein Auto zu kaufen.
structures.ex2_ref: She saves money in order to buy a car.

structures.title: Passive voice
structures.explanation: The passive focuses on the action rather than the doer: conjugated werden in position two and the Partizip II at the end. Name the agent, if needed, with von + dative.
structures.ex2_target: Das Haus wird von einer Firma gebaut.
structures.ex2_ref: The house is being built by a company.

structures.title: Perfect tense (spoken past)
structures.explanation: The everyday past tense uses haben or sein in position two and the past participle at the end. Movement and change-of-state verbs take sein; all others take haben.
structures.ex2_ref: We drove / have driven to Berlin.

structures.title: Superlative (the most …)
structures.explanation: For the highest degree use am + adjective + -sten as a predicate, or der/die/das …-ste before a noun. Many adjectives add an umlaut, and gut/viel are irregular.
structures.ex1_target: Im Winter ist es am kältesten.

structures.title: Concession with obwohl (although)
structures.explanation: obwohl (although) introduces a subordinate clause with the verb at the end. If that clause comes first, the following main clause begins with its verb, keeping the verb in second position overall.
structures.ex1_target: Obwohl es regnet, gehe ich raus.
structures.ex1_ref: Although it is raining, I am going out.
structures.ex2_target: Ich komme, obwohl ich müde bin.
structures.ex2_ref: I am coming although I am tired.
